Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failure of the test `org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.jdom.JDOMModelTest.testAxisAttribute` is related to handling namespaced attributes with wildcard queries in the XPath expression. The current bug report states that an expression such as `xml/@*` on a namespaced XML element `<xml xmlns:x='foo' x:pop='a'/>` returns null for selectSingleNode(), whereas `@x:*` works correctly. The report suspects the issue is in the DOMAttributeIterator's logic that determines whether an attribute matches the query wildcard.

Looking at the constructor of `DOMAttributeIterator`, when the attribute name has a wildcard (`*`), it iterates over all attributes and filters them via `testAttr(attr)`. The method `testAttr(Attr attr)` tests each attribute for matching conditions. This method obtains the attribute's prefix (`nodePrefix`) and local name (`nodeLocalName`) and compares them against the query name's prefix (`testPrefix`) and local name (`testLocalName`).

If the query wildcard is `*` for local name and the prefix matches the node prefix (checked at line 84: `if (equalStrings(testPrefix, nodePrefix))`), it returns true. If not, it goes on to check namespace URIs associated with the prefixes.

The key point pointed out by the bug report is that if `testPrefix` is `null` (which it will be when the XPath is `@*` with no prefix, i.e., a wildcard for all attributes regardless of prefix), the check `if (equalStrings(testPrefix, nodePrefix))` will fail because `testPrefix` is null and `nodePrefix` might not be null. This causes the method to skip matching attributes that have a prefix, hence missing namespaced attributes when selecting all attributes by wildcard, which leads to no results for `xml/@*`.

The report suggests changing the code from:
```
if (equalStrings(testPrefix, nodePrefix)) {
    return true;
}
```
to:
```
if (testPrefix == null || equalStrings(testPrefix, nodePrefix)) {
    return true;
}
```
This fix implies that if the query has no prefix (wildcard for any prefix), any attribute prefix will be accepted, allowing namespaced attributes to be matched with the wildcard selector.

This diagnosis aligns with the failure of the test, which expects to match namespaced attributes via wildcard `@*` but currently fails, and is consistent with the code structure of `DOMAttributeIterator.testAttr`.

Recent reports do not add additional relevant information; thus, the core fix is to update the prefix matching logic in `DOMAttributeIterator.testAttr`.

Final diagnosis: The bug is that `DOMAttributeIterator.testAttr` method does not accept attributes with any prefix when the query prefix is null (wildcard `@*`). It incorrectly requires the test prefix (from the XPath name) and node prefix (attribute prefix) to be equal, missing attributes with prefixes. Changing the condition to accept any node prefix when the test prefix is null resolves the bug and enables namespaced attribute selection with wildcards.

The problematic method is `DOMAttributeIterator.testAttr(org.w3c.dom.Attr)`.
